learn.prompt: A 12 V source supplies 2 A. How much power is delivered?

misconceptionMap.a: You divided voltage by current. Power multiplies them.
misconceptionMap.c: You doubled the product. P = V I, not 2 V I.
misconceptionMap.d: That is V², not V I.

learn.prompt: A 6 V source drives 0.5 A. Set the power.
A 3 A current flows through a 4 Ω resistor. Enter the power dissipated in watts.
learn.hint: You do not know the voltage directly. Use P = I² R.

check.prompt: A 9 V source drives 0.5 A. What power is delivered?

misconceptionMap.a: You squared the current. P = V I.
misconceptionMap.c: You added the numbers instead of multiplying them.
misconceptionMap.d: You divided by 0.5 instead of multiplying by it.

check.prompt: A 12 V source is across a 4 Ω resistor. Enter the power in watts.
check.hint: Find the current first, or use P = V² / R.

takeaway.title: Power is the rate of energy transfer
takeaway.body: P = V I. With Ohm's law this becomes P = I² R = V² / R. Choose the form that uses the quantities you already know.
